MongoDB stores documents in collections. Use `oauth_db_mongodb()` to read
those documents, calculate summaries with aggregation pipelines and issue
database commands using each visitor's permissions.

This helper uses MongoDB's official Python driver, PyMongo, through
reticulate. MongoDB must accept workforce OIDC access tokens from your
identity provider. This requires an eligible Atlas deployment or MongoDB
Enterprise on Linux; Community Server doesn't provide workforce OIDC.

## Before running the app

Install reticulate and configure a Python environment before starting Shiny:

```{r install}
install.packages("reticulate")

reticulate::virtualenv_create("shiny-mongodb")
reticulate::py_install(c("pymongo>=4.10", "numpy"), envname = "shiny-mongodb")
reticulate::use_virtualenv("shiny-mongodb", required = TRUE)
```

Use the same Python environment on your app server. You can also select its
interpreter with `RETICULATE_PYTHON` in `.Renviron`, before R starts. The
helper initializes Python only when a signed-in visitor first queries data.

| Setting | Where to get it |
| --- | --- |
| `OAUTHDB_MONGODB_URL` | The cluster's connection string, without credentials, a database path or authentication/TLS/retry options |
| `OAUTHDB_MONGODB_DATABASE` | The database containing your collections |
| `OAUTHDB_MONGODB_ISSUER` | Exact HTTPS issuer trusted by MongoDB |
| `OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID`, `OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET` | A web OAuth registration at that provider, with the app's redirect URI |
| OAuth scopes and audience | Your identity provider's registration for MongoDB; the example `database.read` scope must exist or be replaced |

For a private CA, supply its certificate file through `ca_bundle`. With
`mongodb://`, the default token host allowlist contains the seed hosts.
Replica members must also be allowed. For Atlas SRV URLs such as
`mongodb+srv://cluster0.abc.mongodb.net`, the default is `*.abc.mongodb.net`.
Other SRV deployments require an explicit `allowed_hosts` vector.

## A complete app

The provider must issue JWT access tokens with the audience MongoDB expects.
Configure provider-specific audience parameters on your shinyOAuth provider
when needed. Use your collection name and filter in the query below.

After signing in,
click **Load rows**. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

issuer <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_MONGODB_ISSUER")

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(issuer = issuer)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "database.read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),

    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),

  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )

  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  mongo <- oauth_db_mongodb(
    auth$connection,
    url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_MONGODB_URL"),
    db = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_MONGODB_DATABASE"),
    issuer = issuer,
    client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID")
  )

  query_task <- oauth_db_task(mongo, method = "find")

  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke("orders", filter = "{\"country\":\"NL\"}", limit = 20)
  })

  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)

    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.
```

## MongoDB and provider setup

Configure [Atlas workforce federation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/workforce-oidc/)
or [MongoDB Enterprise workforce OIDC](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/oidc/workforce/configure-oidc/).
MongoDB must trust the issuer and audience, map the JWT principal or groups
to database users or roles, and grant access to the required collections.
For self-managed deployments, MongoDB documents workforce support from
7.0.11; consult its version and platform requirements before deployment.

Register the Shiny app at that provider with its own redirect URI. The app
uses shinyOAuth for browser sign-in and token renewal. MongoDB's human OIDC
challenge must advertise the configured issuer and, when `client_id` is
supplied, that client ID. If multiple providers require a username to select
one, set `user` to that username or a function returning it for the selected
account.

The Python callback supplies only the visitor's existing access token. It
doesn't launch a second browser flow, obtain workload credentials, or use
the host's cloud account. Token and username changes replace the cached
client on its next use. Sign-out, permission loss and session end close it.

The helper always enables certificate and hostname verification. URL options
are restricted to deployment and query settings such as `replicaSet`,
`directConnection`, `readPreference` and `w`. Configure credentials, CA trust
and timeouts with the helper's arguments.

## Queries, BSON values and commands

Filters, projections and pipelines are JSON strings. PyMongo's BSON parser
also accepts Extended JSON, so object identifiers and other BSON types can
be supplied without converting them to ordinary strings:

```{r queries}
mongo$find("orders", filter = '{"_id":{"$oid":"507f1f77bcf86cd799439011"}}')

mongo$aggregate(
  "orders",
  '[
  {"$match":{"country":"NL"}},
  {"$group":{"_id":"$category","total":{"$sum":"$amount"}}}
]'
)

mongo$count("orders", filter = '{"country":"NL"}')
mongo$run('{"connectionStatus":1}')
```

Reads consume and close their cursors within the operation, including result
pages. `find()` defaults to 100 documents; set `limit = 0` to read all matches.
Use `simplify = FALSE` for lists instead of data frames. Object identifiers,
dates, binary values and other BSON-specific types retain their Extended
JSON representation. Large integers are strings to preserve their exact value.

`run()` returns one native command response. It can issue writes when the
visitor has permission, but excludes authentication, transaction and cursor
commands. Use `find()` and `aggregate()` for cursor results. Inspect native
write response fields such as `writeErrors` when issuing batch write commands.
There is no DBI connection, live cursor or transaction handle.

Driver retryable reads and writes are disabled. The wrapper doesn't replay
failed queries or commands. PyMongo may perform protocol reauthentication
with the same supplied token. A timeout or sign-out doesn't guarantee that
the server stops work already submitted, including `$out` or `$merge` stages.

## Compatibility checks

The repository's [MongoDB fixture](https://github.com/lukakoning/shinyOAuthDB/tree/main/integration/mongodb-oidc)
checks the driver, token validation, permissions and TLS with disposable
credentials. It is separate from browser OAuth and a live Atlas deployment.
